label: early original-phase run of tokens from {a,d,f,i,l,m,n,o,p,r,s}
predicate: (t <= 2) & isin(in_tok, [tok(c) for c in "adfilmnoprs"]) & (n_seen([tok(c) for c in "adfilmnoprs"]) == t)
explanation: Fires only in the first three original-phase input steps (t=0..2; essentially never at t>=3, the delimiter, or the copy phase) when the current input and every input before it belong to the letter set {a,d,f,i,l,m,n,o,p,r,s}. At t=0 a token from the set gives the unit with precision 1.0. At t=1/t=2 it stays on only if the prefix is also all from the set; one outside token earlier (e.g. t, c, q, h) turns it off. Magnitude depends on the token: o, a, i, n, l carry the most mass and d, s, r, m the least, and the largest values come at t=1 (e.g. o after i). Weak exceptions: it fires weakly on k, w, x, 1 when they follow a set token, and the set also tolerates a leading v. Never fires on b, c, e, g, h, j, q, t, u, y, 0, 2, 3. Rate falls with L only because the active positions are a fixed early window.

issues: The claim that one earlier token from outside the set turns the unit off is wrong for x and v. At t=1, a set token after a leading x fires with precision 1.0 (1210 steps, 6.9% of the top activation quartile), and after a leading v also with precision 1.0. A leading 1 fires with precision 0.76. These are strong, systematic activations, not the 'weak exceptions' the explanation describes.
The explanation says v was added to the set, but the reported predicate does not contain v. The label and predicate also leave out x and 1 as tolerated preceding tokens.

The explanation lists x and 1 among tokens that fire 'weakly' as the current input. They are not: as current-token predicates they score near zero. Their real role is as preceding tokens, which the explanation mixes up.

The other claims hold. The original phase carries 100% of the activation mass; t=0..2 carries all of it apart from 48 steps at t=3. A set token at t=0 has precision 1.0. No t=0 token outside the set fires. The ordering of activation mass across tokens is as described.

Adding x, v and 1 to the tolerated prefix raises test F1 from 0.898 to 0.934 and mass recall from 0.874 to 0.964. The remaining misses (w or h before the token, k as the current token) and false positives at t=2 are minor.
